login.note: Medium prefers passwordless: Google/Facebook/Apple/X SSO, or an emailed magic sign-in link with no password at all. The magic-link path means the human needs their mailbox open, and the link must be opened IN THIS PROFILE's browser or the session lands somewhere else.

logout.note: Hitting it navigates to the signed-out home page. It clears the medium.com session only — a custom-domain publication the profile signed into separately may keep its own.

traps: `sid` is HttpOnly so document.cookie cannot see the live session, AND `uid` is left behind after sign-out so document.cookie can claim a session that no longer exists. Cookies are wrong in both directions here — this is the worst site in this set to cookie-check.
Cloudflare fronts medium.com and answers a plain non-browser request with HTTP 403 (observed here 2026-09-12). Reads must run inside the real browser; curl-style fetching is not a fallback.
The internal /_/api/* endpoints prefix their JSON with an XSSI guard (`])}while(1);</x>`), so response.json() throws on a completely healthy reply. Read text, cut to the first '{'.

Publication custom domains (and *.medium.com publications) render a different app shell. The Apollo state keys the probe looks for may simply not exist there, so always probe medium.com itself, never the article's vanity domain.

Medium's inline state global has changed name over the years (__APOLLO_STATE__, __PRELOADED_STATE__, __NEXT_DATA__). The probe tries the first two and falls through to the API rather than trusting any single one.
notes: Probe strategy (a) then (b) then a deliberately-labelled-weak (c). (a) is Medium's inline Apollo cache: ROOT_QUERY.viewer resolves through __ref to the User record with the username, and an explicit null viewer is the site stating it is signed out. (b) is a credentialed same-origin GET of Medium's own who-am-I, /_/api/users/self, with the XSSI prefix stripped — it is checked for payload.user, not for a 200. (c) is a header-avatar DOM check, used only when both of the above fail and flagged in `why` as weak so nobody mistakes it for evidence. Cookies are never consulted (see traps). UNVERIFIED and the least certain of the four: medium.com answered 403 to every unauthenticated inspection from this machine, so the state-object key names and the users/self payload shape are both hypotheses from documentation and prior art. A live `verify` should print the actual globals first. A READ recipe should replay Medium's GraphQL rather than parse HTML: the app POSTs to https://medium.com/_/graphql with a `graphql-operation` header naming the query (feed, post and user queries all go through it) — capture one real request with recipe-builder and replay it; the same XSSI/403 traps apply.
probe_checked: positive path PROVEN live 2026-09-12: ran in the fork against a signed-in session and returned a handle from the site's own state global.
